key_insight: ReLMem learns to update a fixed-size patient memory over time, letting a frozen LLM model longitudinal EHRs without rereading the full history.
clinical_relevance: This could make long-patient-history prediction tasks, such as medication prediction, more efficient by reducing storage and compute while preserving useful clinical context.
method: Uses lightweight compression adapters to recurrently merge each new visit into an existing memory.
Trains with multi-granularity supervision to match compressed-memory attention to full-history attention.
Adds prediction supervision on the final memory for downstream task performance.
evidence_signal: On EHR medication prediction, ReLMem nearly matched a full-history baseline while cutting retained historical storage by 97.1% and improved macro-/micro-F1 by 4.66/4.75 points over the strongest compressed-memory baseline.
watch_item: Results are reported on a specific EHR prediction setting, so performance and robustness may differ across institutions, tasks, and memory budgets.
paper_title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling
